newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, MAY 12 - SUNDAY, MAY 18.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, MAY 12 - SUNDAY, MAY 18.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS

BRUSSELS - EU finance ministers meet (Monday); review which countries have deficits and debt out of line with the Maastricht treaty economic convergence criteria for a single currency; review Spain and Portugal's economic convergence programmes.

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (Monday-Friday); debates a code of conduct for EU lobbyists, EU energy and environment policies, the defence industry and security policy, the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms. Commissioner Bonino presents European Commission's communication on food safety to the BSE follow-up committee (Wednesday).
STRASBOURG - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday).
BRUSSELS - EU research ministers meet (Wednesday-Thursday).
STRASBOURG - Former Russian security chief Alexander Lebed meets European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles (Wednesday) (to be confirmed).

AMSTERDAM - EU Committee of the Regions holds first summit of the regions and cities (Thursday-Friday). Discussions focus on structural funds, enlargement, employment, inter-governmental conference. Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, European Commission President Jacques Santer also attend. Opening news conference on Thursday; closing news conference on Friday.
MONDAY, MAY 12
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU finance ministers meet. Agenda includes:
- Convergence programme for Portugal and Spain.
- Commission information on euro coins.
- Commission presentation and exchange of views on 1998 preliminary budget
- Excessive deficit procedure:
- Abrogation of excessive deficits;
- Recommendations to member states with an excessive deficit.
- Commission presentation on the internal market action plan.
- Commission action plan on reform of the customs transit regime.
- Presidency progress report on taxation of energy products.
- Progress report on compaany taxation: extension of parent/subsidiary directive.

- Commission presentation on FISCALIS programme and report on administrative cooperation on VAT. Provisional agenda includes annual EU excessive deficit review, to see which countries have deficits and debt out of line with the Maastricht treaty; review of Spain and Portugal's programmes for fulfilling economic convergence criteria for participating in the single currency.

STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (to Friday). Debates on a code of conduct for EU lobbyists; EU energy and environment policies; trans-European telecommunications networks; EU rules on public contracts; marketing rules for weedkillers, pesticides and other "biocides"; European defence industries; regional cooperation between the countries of ex-Yugoslavia; ratification of the UN Law of the Sea Convention implementation agreement.
Agenda includes:
- (1700/1500 GMT) Anastassopoulos report on satellite and cable TV: decoders and beating the cheats.
- Palacio Vallelersundi report on simple legislation and subsidiarity.
- Ford report on a code of conduct for lobbyists.
- Donnelly report on rule change on voting.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following European Parliament committees meet:
- (1800/1600 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
- (1830/1630 GMT) Budgetary Control;
- (1900/1700 GMT) Agriculture;
Budget - Commissioner Liikanen presents draft 1998 budget;
Energy;
Regional Policy;
Rules of Procedure.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Trade Union Committee for Education holds conference under the patronage of European Commission President Santer on "Teachers in Europe debate their situation" (and Tuesday). The aim of the conference is to promote the dialogue between teachers at a European level. Speakers include: European Commissioner Cresson. Contact: Alain Moucoux (322) 224 0692.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "The IGC and citizens' rights" (1315/1115 GMT) on the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms. Speaker is Euro Citizen Action Service Director Tony Venables. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
NOORDWIJK (NEW ITEM) - Dutch Interior Ministry holds conference on "Crime prevention: towards a European level" (and Tuesday). Venue: Hotel van Oranje.
PARIS - Western European Union ministers meet (and Tuesday).

LONDON - IBC UK Conferences Ltd. holds conference on "EC competition law" (and Tuesday). Topics include: the green paper on vertical restraints and exhaustion of intellectual property rights. Venue: The Hyde Park Hotel. Contact: IBC UK Conferences Ltd. (44) 171 453 2711.

MUNICH - European Air Law Association holds seminar on "Liability claims handling in the airlines and aerospace industries" (1915/1715 GMT). Venue: Kempinski Hotel Airport. Contact: European Air Law Association (49) 89 365 061.
TUESDAY, MAY 13
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (second of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Barthet-Mayer report on organic farming.
- European Commission presents 1998 preliminary draft budget.
- Collins report on reducing pollution.
- Jensen report on health protection and biocides.
- Collins report on EU environmental law.
- Amadeo report on health safety at work - radiation dangers.
- Hoppenstedt report on telecoms TENs.
- Langen report on World Trade Organisation (WTO) and public contracts.
- Todini report on education and mobility.
- Mosiek-Urbahn report on supervising insurance companies.
- (1200/1000 GMT) Votes on reports under the cooperation, co-decision and assent procedures.
- Procedure without report:
- Collective redundancies - Consultation procedure.
- Motions for resolutions on which the debate has closed.
- (1730/1530 GMT) Question time to Commission.
- (1900/1700 GMT) Political group meetings.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following European Parliament committees meet:
- (1730/1530 GMT) External Economic Relations;
Legal Affairs;
Social Affairs;
Youth/Culture;
Institutional Affairs.

HABAY-LA-NEUVE, Belgium - European Commissioner Van Miert addresses Arlon Committee Financial Forum on "Competition: European stakes and perspectives" (1130/0930 GMT). Venue: Salle d'Anlier. Contact: Arlon Committee Financial Forum (32) 63 22 39 87.

METZ, France - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) hosts "Tour for jobs" (to Thursday), when 50 or so riders including trade union leaders will cycle between Metz and Brussels via Petange, Luxembourg, Schengen, Trier, Vaals, Maastricht, Tongeren, Waremme and Louvain. The Luxembourg-Trier stage will be started by 1996 Tour de France victor Bjarne Riis and ETUC Secretary General Emilio Gabaglio.

LONDON - The European Regions Airline Association (ERA) holds third annual crisis management conference (and Wednesday). Discussions will focus on the examination of every element of disaster planning, from the immediate response to longterm considerations. Venue: Ramada Hotel, Heathrow Airport. Contact: ERA (44) 276 856495. 071449 DED:BC-DIARY-WEEKLY =2 Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 2/2 - Wednesday-Friday)
WEDNESDAY, MAY 14

BRUSSELS - EU research ministers meet (and Thursday). Provisional agenda includes structured dialogue with Central and East European ministers, the proposed Fifth Framework Programme on research and development, action plan for innovation, scientific cooperation accord with United States, a European research network.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (1500/1300 GMT). Provisional agenda includes communication on the energy dimension of climate change.
STRASBOURG - Former Russian security chief Alexander Lebed meets European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles (1500/1300 GMT) (to be confirmed).
STRASBOURG - Commissioner Bonino presents European Commission's communication on food safety to the European Parliament's BSE follow-up committee.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (third of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Any objections to the list of motions for resolutions selected for debate.
- (0915/0715 GMT) Council and Commission statement on progress in the inter-governmental conference (IGC) and prospects for agreement at the June Amsterdam summit - followed by a debate.
- Tindemans report on a common security policy.
- Titley report on defence industries - call for cooperation.
- Cohn-Bendit report on rebuilding Bosnia.
- Baron Crespo report on reinforcing the effectiveness of Joint Actions.

- Varela Suanzes-Carpegna, Macartney, Crampton, Teverson and Souchet reports on international fisheries agreements, fishing conservation, NAFO control measures and protocol to the fishing accord with Sao Tome and Principe.
- (1200/1000 GMT) Votes on:
- Reports under cooperation, codecision and assent procedures;
- Motions for resolutions on which the debate has closed.
- (1730/1530 GMT) Question time to the Council.
- (1900/1700 GMT) Political group meetings.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following European Parliament committee meets:
- (1600/1400 GMT) Environment.

STRASBOURG - Verband der Automobilindustrie holds news conference on "Euro-vignette - fair and efficient prices in traffic" (1700/1500 GMT) on EU proposals on road use fees. Venue: Parliamentary Association of the European Parliament. Contact: Verband der Automobilindustrie (49) 89 975 070.
FLORENCE, Italy - European Natural Gas Vehicle Association (ENGVA) holds conference on "Creating the climate for NGVs" (to Friday). Contact: ENGVA (31) 20 597 3100.
THURSDAY, MAY 15

BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts round table on practical aspects of the passage to the euro. Participants include representatives of consumer assocations, small and medium-sized enterprises, banks, unions, national and local administrations.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (fourth of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (until 1000/0800 GMT) Political group meetings.
- (1000/0800 GMT) Stockmann report on common energy policy.
- Soulier report on the future of nuclear power.
- Rothe report on the future of renewables.
- Holm report on energy cooperation with Asia.
- Redondo Jimenez report on improving agriculture.
- Votes on:
- Reports under the cooperation, codecision and assent procedures;
- Motions for resolutions on which the debate has closed.

BRUSSELS - European Commissioner Bonino attends Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) Environment Section meeting (1430/1230 GMT); discusses Commission restructuring to deal with food safety and green paper on food law. Venue: ECOSOC, 2 rue Ravenstein.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "EU competition policy - What next?" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is European Commission Directorate-General IV (Competition) official Jonathan Faull. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
BRUGES, Belgium - European grain lobby COCERAL holds congress to celebrate its 40th anniversary (to Saturday). Contact: Chantal Fauth (322) 502 0808.

AMSTERDAM - EU Committee of the Regions holds first summit of the regions and cities (1600/1400 GMT) (and Friday). Discussions focus on structural funds, enlargement, employment, inter-governmental conference. Speakers include: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, European Commission President Jacques Santer, European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles, Committee of the Regions President Pasqual Maragall. Opening news conference at 1830/1630 GMT. Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155.
FRIDAY, MAY 16
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (last of five days).
Agenda includes:

- (0900/0700 GMT) Joint debate on Rack report on the implementation of EU regional policy in Austria, Finland and Sweden and Myller report on regional policy, cross-border cooperation and enlargement.
- Medina Ortega reports on international trade marks.
AMSTERDAM - EU Committee of the Regions summit of regions and cities (second of two days). Closing news conference at 1800/1600 GMT.
SATURDAY, MAY 17

GENEVA - The International Telecommunications Union celebrates World Telecommunications Day - "Telecommunications and humanitarian assistance", commemorating its founding in Paris 132 years ago. Contact: International Telecommunications Union (41) 22 730 5111.
SUNDAY, MAY 18
- Whit Sunday.
